title: coax names its agent to decade and reports the agent's state
body:
`connect_decade` in `src/app.rs` joins the decade socket with `Channel::from_env("coax", &[], &[], None)`. The last argument is an `Option<&Agent>` that coax leaves empty, so decade does not know an agent runs in coax's pane.

decade's protocol (`../decade/docs/protocol.md`, the hello section and "Agents") lets a client that runs an agent name it in hello as `Agent { name, version, session }`. The client then reports on it with `agent` messages carrying `AgentUpdate` fields: `state` (`idle`, `working`, `done`, `attention`), `activity`, `question`, `model`, `context`, `tokens` and `cost`. decade uses the state to badge workspaces and to raise a desktop notification.

coax has most of this already. `app::run` connects after the ACP session opens, so the agent's name (`App::agent`), its reported version (`agent_info.version`) and the session ID are all known by then. `Transcript::in_flight` and the permission prompt map onto `working` and `attention`.

## Open

- The decade-channel API was uncommitted and still changing on 2026-11-08. Recheck it before building on it.
- Which ACP events map to `activity`, and whether coax can fill `model`, `context`, `tokens` or `cost` from anything the adapter sends.
- Jack has more uses for the socket in mind that have not been discussed yet.
